status: All54 focused native executions and338 tooling tests pass. BBC production eligibility, original references and matched unprofiled instructions pending; no saving or catalog credit.

focused.initial_failures: Initial aggregator mistakes an import line inside an embedded JS program for a V module import and runs no tests. The refined fixture incorrectly keeps an escaped regexp as a call candidate and requires every Unicode form to be rewritten. Both candidate and word-only control fail these fixture assumptions. Corrected checks compare exact trusted-lexer output for every possible call and require real dynamic imports to execute with expected module contents, URL counts and cache behavior in all six forms, including BOM and Unicode line separators. All final cases pass without changing the filter.

implementation: Classic scripts with an import word use a conservative following-token rejection filter. Skip ASCII whitespace and closed block/ASCII line comments; keep a following opening parenthesis, dot, any non-ASCII byte, incomplete comment or possible HTML comment on the trusted lexer path. Do not lex strings/regex/preceding tokens. Invalid static imports remain unchanged for the original JSC classic parser to reject; all module scripts retain the original lexer. Separate control retains word-only filtering.
qualification: No source URL, author script bytes, scripting policy, capture endpoint, reference/tolerance, layout or rendering policy changes. Native tests require actual imported values, cached single URL fetch, exact trusted-lexer transforms on Unicode/comment forms, classic syntax errors, module maps/cycles/live exports/top-level await and original Promise rejection behavior in both arms. Failed fixture assumptions are retained without engine changes.

storage.purpose: Losslessly compress only completed, independently guarded generated BBC test executables, never browser bundles, shared build receipts, sources or raw measurement evidence. Every compressed byte stream is decoded/hash-verified before removing its duplicate; restore executable bytes/mode before rerunning a historical command.
